title: SK hynix denies playing hardball with Trump admin over 3D NAND fab — report claimed company demanded increased chipmaking equipment exports to China in exchange for US fab (updated)
source_used: Tom's Hardware (update with SK hynix statement, 16 Oct 2026 6am ET)
key_facts: Update of 16 Oct 2026: SK hynix issued a statement to Tom's Hardware that no capacity expansion is being sought for the Dalian Mod B, completed in 2023.
The statement says equipment installation for Mod B is carried out in close consultation with and under authorisation from the US government.
The original report (Reuters, 15 Oct 2026): SK hynix is asking the US to authorise more chipmaking tool shipments to Dalian in exchange for a commitment to build a new US NAND fab.
The Dalian fab makes 192-layer floating-gate 3D NAND for Solidigm's data-centre SSDs; its tools come from Applied Materials, KLA and Lam Research and need US licences.
Last December Commerce gave SK hynix a limited authorisation for Dalian equipment for 2026 but has not issued one for 2027, per Reuters.
Solidigm wants to install tools in the unused part of Mod B; Tom's Hardware notes that, as the building was completed in 2023, this is not a capacity expansion.
Solidigm is considering an IPO as early as 2027.
quote_evidence: No capacity expansion is being sought for the Dalian Mod B, which was completed in 2023.
The installation of equipment for Mod B is being carried out in close consultation with and under authorization from the U.S. government.
Solidigm has requested U.S. export licenses for additional tools, but the U.S. government has yet to authorize the shipments.
why_it_matters_hint: SK hynix publicly contests the framing of the Reuters report; US limits on tools for Chinese fabs are tight.
event_date: Reuters report 15 Oct 2026; SK hynix statement 16 Oct 2026
notes: Follow-up of 1015:C08-01 (item 42 of our 15 Oct 2026 edition), which already carried SK hynix's earlier denial to Reuters that it seeks to expand capacity. New today: the written statement to Tom's Hardware naming Mod B (completed 2023). The statement does not address the claimed exchange of tool exports for a US fab.
